== APPRAISAL INSTRUCTIONS (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task D; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §§1-2; APPRAISAL_FORM.md; CODEBOOK.md §8) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:

NEVER guess study design or bias ratings from citation/title!

2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not assessable — Secondary single-country institutional case study synthesizing published cross-sectional surveys, scientific water-quality studies, and historical accounts with no primary cohort or participant follow-up.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern — Mentions historical infrastructure decay and debt from the 1970s-1980s, rapid urbanisation (from ~30% to >40% between 1990 and 2008), population/tourism/industrial demand growth, and bi-directional neighbourhood-income poverty, but uses no analytical or empirical strategy to disentangle these confounders from commercialisation or the 2005-2011 AVRL management contract.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Weak to moderate — Clearly maps PPP contractual forms (Table 1) and institutional restructuring (GWSC to GWCL in 1998, CWSA rural decoupling, PURC creation in 1997, AVRL management contract 2005-2011, GUWCL in 2011), but relies on secondary accounts rather than primary legal/contractual instruments, inconsistently cites the PURC enabling statute as both Act 538 (1997) and Act 578 on the same page (PDF Page 9, p. 1142), and conflates the implemented management contract with affermage in the concluding critique (PDF Page 9, p. 1142).
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate to high concern — Establishes a clear multidimensional distinction between wide coverage and deep access (quality, reliability, cost, equitable distribution) using cited secondary metrics, but relies uncritically on heterogeneous secondary sources (including operator web pages, unpublished theses, and news portals) without auditing primary measurement validity or sample denominators.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Moderate — Strong conceptual disaggregation of urban water outcomes across MDG coverage, microbial/chemical contamination, continuity and per-capita daily volume (litres/day), official tariff versus tanker-market pricing and household expenditure shares, and wealth-quintile/neighbourhood connection equity, but entirely dependent on secondary studies whose primary measurement procedures and sampling frames are not verified.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: High concern — No pre-specified protocol, literature search strategy, or source-inclusion rules; narrative assembly of secondary statistics and illustrative examples creates substantial risk of selective reporting aligned with the paper's critique of market-oriented water reform.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern — Purposive choice of Ghana as an illustrative national case is explicitly justified, but there is no documented search strategy or selection protocol governing which secondary surveys, scientific studies, dissertations, and media reports within Ghana were included or excluded.

domain_ratings.justification: Cites the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission Act, Act 538, 1997, PURC (2005) Urban Water Tariff Policy, National Urban Policy (2010), and UN General Comment No. 15 (2002), but exhibits internal legal/institutional inaccuracies: on PDF Page 9 (p. 1142) it cites Act 538, 1997 and four sentences later refers to the same statutory mandate as Act 578 without explanation; it also documents on PDF Page 6 (p. 1139) that Ghana abandoned affermage for a management contract with AVRL, yet on PDF Page 9 (p. 1142) repeatedly describes Ghana's implemented PPP with AVRL as affermage. Relies primarily on secondary literature rather than primary statutory or contractual texts.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Obeng-Odoom (2012) is a single-country political-economy and institutional-historical case study of urban water governance in Ghana (1957-2011) that synthesizes secondary histories, official statistics, scientific water-quality studies, and statutory/regulatory provisions without primary fieldwork, a comparator arm, or a systematic review search protocol. Appraised under the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework (as a structured non-validated judgment rather than a numeric score), the paper demonstrates strong jurisdictional specificity (D2), strong conceptual outcome definition distinguishing MDG coverage ("wide access") from quality, reliability, affordability, and distributional equity ("deep access") (D4), and strong political-economy institutional contextualisation of GWSC/GWCL restructuring, donor conditionality, civil society contestation, CWSA decoupling, and PURC-GWCL-AVRL regulatory asymmetries (D10), alongside adequate PPP exposure classification (D3) and secondary metric reporting (D7). However, methodological rigour for empirical and causal inference is severely constrained by the absence of a documented literature search or source-selection protocol (D5, D6, D11), lack of counterfactual causal identification or confounding adjustment separating the 2005-2011 AVRL management contract from long-standing infrastructure deficits and rapid urban growth (D8, D9), absence of methodological reflexivity (D13), and weak legal/institutional citation precision on p. 1142—where the PURC statute is cited first as Act 538 (1997) and four sentences later as Act 578, and where AVRL's arrangement is repeatedly referred to as affermage despite p. 1139 documenting that affermage was abandoned in favour of a management contract (D1).
raw_response.overall_rating: Structured non-validated judgment: High methodological concern for causal/empirical inference (strong conceptual outcome framing, jurisdictional specificity, and institutional context; adequate exposure classification and secondary measurement reporting; weak legal citation precision, sampling/selection transparency, causal identification, confounding control, replication potential, and reflexivity; coding not assessable)
raw_response.study_design_identified: Single-country institutional and political-economy historical case study synthesizing secondary survey, water-quality, and statutory/regulatory sources (no primary empirical data collection or systematic literature search)
raw_response.where_found_summary: Case framing and aims on PDF Page 3 (p. 1136, Introduction); institutional and PPP history on PDF Pages 4-6 (pp. 1137-1139, Modern history of urban water provision in Ghana, including Table 1); secondary empirical synthesis on coverage, quality, reliability, cost, and equity on PDF Pages 6-8 (pp. 1139-1141, Access to water) and Note 2 on PDF Page 10 (p. 1143); statutory discussion of PURC (Act 538 / Act 578) and policy conclusions on PDF Pages 8-10 (pp. 1141-1143, Lessons, implications, and concluding remarks); bibliography and author note on PDF Pages 10-13 (pp. 1143-1146). No dedicated Methods section is present.
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: The paper explicitly frames itself as a single-country institutional-historical case study of urban water governance and access in Ghana (1957-2011), tracing public utility restructuring (GWSC to GWCL), PPP contract selection (AVRL 2005-2011 management contract), and statutory regulation (PURC Act 538, 1997) alongside secondary empirical evidence. It fits none of the six conventional empirical checklists: there is no randomization (RoB 2), no comparator arm or quasi-experimental design (single-case histories without a comparator cannot be assigned to ROBINS-I), no primary cross-sectional or cohort dataset analysed (JBI), no primary qualitative fieldwork/interviews (CASP/MMAT), and no systematic search protocol (AMSTAR 2 is prohibited for non-systematic narrative reviews). The Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework directly matches this institutional/legal-historical case study design while capturing its secondary-source selection, confounding, and statutory accuracy limitations.
